question.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}[{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{1}{y{cos}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{1}{y}[{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{1}{y}[{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}{sec}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{1}{y}[\operatorname{tan}⁡x]_{0}^{\pi /4}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{1}{y}(\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})-\operatorname{tan}⁡0)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{1}{y}\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

 

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{1}{y}\,\text{d}y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|y|{|}_{1}^{e} \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡e-\operatorname{ln}⁡1 \\  & =1-0 \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$
